title: Fix the Lambda With the Wrong Parameter Count
description: The program should use a lambda to implement a functional interface that compares two integers.
expectedBehavior: The program should compile and print the result of comparing 3 and 5.
actualProblem: The Comparer interface's single abstract method takes two parameters, but the lambda (a) -> a only declares one. Java rejects this at compile time because the lambda's parameter count doesn't match the functional interface's method signature.
explanation: A lambda expression must match the parameter count (and compatible types) of the functional interface's single abstract method exactly, since the lambda is essentially providing that method's implementation.
